recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what the modulus becomes on the side you are approaching from, and what is left to substitute.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Use |x| = x on the right side
steps.margin_note: First mark. State |x| = x for x > 0 before cancelling anything. The examiner is checking that the one-sided arrow was read.

recall.must_convey: That for x > 0 the modulus gives |x| = x, so the term 2|x|/x is the constant 2.
accept: on the right side x is positive so mod x equals x
the first term becomes two x over x which is two
x is greater than zero so the modulus comes off unchanged
right hand limit kabatti mod x equals x, so two vasthundi
remove the modulus using x positive and get two

steps.why: The side of approach decides the answer. On the right side x is positive, so |x| = x and the first term is simply the constant 2.
common_mistakes: Writing |x| = −x, which is the rule for the LEFT side.
Cancelling x/x at x = 0 itself; a limit only uses values with x ≠ 0.
steps.memory_tip: Read the small plus sign first: plus means x stays on the positive side, so the modulus bars come off unchanged.

steps.label: Substitute x = 0
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Box the 3. The two-sided limit does not exist here — the left-hand value is −1 — so keep the ⁺ on every line.
lines: So for x > 0 the expression is  2 + x + 1 = x + 3

lines.text: (the two expressions are equal for x > 0)
(x + 3 is a polynomial, so put x = 0)

recall.must_convey: That the expression reduces to x + 3 and its limit at 0 is 3.
accept: what is left is x plus three so the limit is three
substitute zero into x plus three and get three
two plus zero plus one is three
x plus three lo zero pettina three vasthundi

steps.why: Once the modulus is removed the expression is the polynomial x + 3, which is continuous, so the limit is its value at x = 0.
common_mistakes: Giving 1, by dropping the 2 that came from the modulus term.
Giving −1, which is the LEFT-hand limit, where 2|x|/x = −2.
steps.memory_tip: The 3 is 2 from the modulus term plus 1 from the constant; the x term contributes nothing at 0.
lines_compact: So for x > 0 the expression is  2 + x + 1 = x + 3

insider_note: From the right x is POSITIVE, so |x| = x and 2|x|/x is simply 2. The rest is substitution: 2 + 0 + 1 = 3.
